about.text: Erzincan tulum is a skin-ripened tulum cheese from Eastern Anatolia, Turkey.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Erzincan tulum is ripened in a goatskin by the milk's own lactic bacteria. A trial that added a yoghurt-type starter to pasteurised ewe's milk shortened the making from 10-12 days to about 2.

steps.name: drain
steps.note: The curd is strained in cloth.

steps.name: press
steps.note: Pressed and drained about 10 days, in the traditional run 10-12 days.

steps.name: pack
steps.note: Packed into a cleaned goatskin that is sewn shut.
No culture is added in the traditional method; the raw milk's own lactic flora ferments it.
With rennet; commercial liquid rennet in the Akkaraman sheep-milk studies.

processing.text: Ripened in a goatskin at altitude. A quick method adds 0.5 % starter (Streptococcus salivarius subsp. thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus 1:1) to pasteurised ewe's milk and cuts making from 10-12 days to about 2.

facts.v: Goatskin (tulum), or plastic or metal boxes today

A trial with 0.5 % starter (1:1 Streptococcus salivarius subsp. thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus) in ewe's milk pasteurised at 65 °C for 30 min cut manufacture from 10-12 days to about 2 days; sensory scores like the traditional cheese
